title: What of Braun's bit-PHP argument transfers to bit LeftPigeon
claim: For the binary left-pigeon principle LP_n (n = 2^l holes, n + 1 pigeons, hole rows of l + 1 bits): (Lemma 1) substituting g(h) := sum_x [f_x = h] x sends every axiom to a sum of bit-PHP collisions, so a pigeon-row polynomial derived from LP_n in degree B is derived from Braun's compact base in degree max(lB, 2l), and Braun's row-linear separation gives pigeon-row separation for LP_n through B <= (n + 1)/(2l); (Theorem 2) Braun's generic criterion applies to LP_n with its own clauses as the covering family, and if the row-linear space over all rows is separated at degree k(12l + 2), every dag-like Res(xor) refutation has 3S + n(n + 1)(l + 1) >= exp(k^2/(3n) - 2) (l >= 4, k <= n/2); (Lemma 3) the hole sums sum_h g_h,j (plus a constant) are in the substitution's kernel, so Lemma 1 cannot separate them; (Lemma 4) the pigeon rows alone are too thin for the criterion at every k Lemma 1 reaches. So B100 reduces to one statement: row-linear separation over all rows of LP_n at degree k(12l + 2) for some k = omega(sqrt(n log n)).
failure_conditions: An LP_n axiom whose image under g := G is not the stated sum of collisions.
A pigeon assignment on which sum_h G(h)_j is not c_j.
A pair (l, k) where Theorem 2's density inequality fails.
A k in Lemma 1's range where the pigeon-row bound reaches 1.
foundation_claim_scope: The octahedral knot sphere's Kasteleyn-signed NAE formula NAE(K_k); proof complexity of its refutations.
